Let
\[
f(g)=7^{c(g)}\qquad(g\in S_6).
\]
The matrix is the group convolution matrix
\[
A_{\sigma,\tau}=f(\sigma^{-1}\tau),
\]
so its determinant is the determinant of right-convolution by the central group-algebra element
\[
C=\sum_{g\in S_6}7^{c(g)}g.
\]

For \(S_n\), the Jucys-Murphy identity gives
\[
\sum_{g\in S_n}x^{c(g)}g
=\prod_{k=1}^n\left(x+\sum_{i<k}(ik)\right).
\]
Indeed, when adding \(n\), either \(n\) is a fixed point, contributing the factor \(x\), or \(n\) is inserted after one of \(1,\dots,n-1\) in an existing cycle, contributing one transposition \((i\,n)\).

On the irreducible representation indexed by a partition \(\lambda\vdash n\), this central element acts by the scalar
\[
\theta_\lambda(x)=\prod_{(i,j)\in\lambda}(x+j-i),
\]
the product over all boxes of the Young diagram. The regular representation contains the irreducible \(\lambda\) with multiplicity \(f^\lambda\), where \(f^\lambda\) is its dimension. Hence
\[
\det A=\prod_{\lambda\vdash 6}\theta_\lambda(7)^{(f^\lambda)^2}.
\]

Now list the partitions of \(6\), their dimensions, and \(\theta_\lambda(7)\):

\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c}
\lambda & f^\lambda & \theta_\lambda(7)\\ \hline
(6)&1&7\cdot8\cdot9\cdot10\cdot11\cdot12\\
(5,1)&5&6\cdot7\cdot8\cdot9\cdot10\cdot11\\
(4,2)&9&6\cdot7^2\cdot8\cdot9\cdot10\\
(4,1,1)&10&5\cdot6\cdot7\cdot8\cdot9\cdot10\\
(3,3)&5&6\cdot7^2\cdot8^2\cdot9\\
(3,2,1)&16&5\cdot6\cdot7^2\cdot8\cdot9\\
(3,1,1,1)&10&4\cdot5\cdot6\cdot7\cdot8\cdot9\\
(2,2,2)&5&5\cdot6^2\cdot7^2\cdot8\\
(2,2,1,1)&9&4\cdot5\cdot6\cdot7^2\cdot8\\
(2,1,1,1,1)&5&3\cdot4\cdot5\cdot6\cdot7\cdot8\\
(1,1,1,1,1,1)&1&2\cdot3\cdot4\cdot5\cdot6\cdot7
\end{array}
\]

The dimension check is
\[
1^2+5^2+9^2+10^2+5^2+16^2+10^2+5^2+9^2+5^2+1^2=720,
\]
so all regular-representation eigenspaces are accounted for.

Collecting prime powers gives
\[
\det A
=
2^{3600}3^{1947}5^{795}7^{1188}11^{26}.
\]

\[
\boxed{2^{3600}3^{1947}5^{795}7^{1188}11^{26}}
\]
